preamble: The voiced retroflex fricative [ʐ] (letter ږ) became the voiced velar stop [g] in the Northeastern dialects of Pashto (Kabul, Peshawar, Jalalabad), in parallel with the shift of [ʂ] to [x]. According to MacKenzie the shift took place in the medieval period, with ẓ̌ going either to palatal [ʝ] (Wardak, Central Ghilji) or to [g] as parallel outcomes. Conservative Southwestern (Kandahar) Pashto keeps [ʐ] and Southeastern dialects have [ʒ]. No comparable ʐ > g change is attested outside Pashto.

examples.note: Kandahar keeps the original [ʐ], so the from-forms show the conservative pronunciation. Southeastern /ʃpaʒ/, Chaki Wardak /ʃpeʝ/.

examples.from: کېږي 3rd sg. present continuous of 'to do', conservative [ʐ] [ˈkeʐi] (kept in southwestern Pashto)
ايږ 'bear', conservative ẓ̌ yiẓ̌ (kept in Kandahar)
مېږی 'ant', conservative ẓ̌ meẓ̌ay (kept in Kandahar)
